title: Applied ML evals: integrated onboarding and regression triage playbook
author: Maya Chen
summary: A single, actionable playbook that ties together the eval harness, prompt sets & benchmarks, model onboarding steps, quality guardrails, quantization profile validation, and regression triage procedures. Intended for ML engineers, evaluation owners, and SREs responsible for model rollouts and quality monitoring.
body:
Purpose:
This document defines the integrated process we use at Redwood Inference to onboard models into the eval harness, author and maintain prompt sets & benchmarks, validate quantization profiles, enforce quality guardrails, and run regression triage when evaluations detect degradation. It is both a how-to guide and an operational playbook for on-call engineers and model owners.

Audience and scope:
- Audience: ML engineers, applied ML, SREs, product owners, and QA engineers.
- Scope: Inference-serving model variants (e.g., fp16, int8 quantized variants), prompt-driven generation and classification tasks, embedding-based signals used in product gating, and automated CI/monitoring pipelines.

Ownership & escalation:
- Evaluation owner: the ML engineer listed on the model's onboarding PR (primary contact for quality questions).
- Observability owner: eng-platform team (dashboards/alerting).
- On-call escalation: follow standard eng-sre incident process; pager for degraded evals is assigned to the SRE rotation first, then to the model owner if no action within 1 hour.

Key signals and thresholds (detectable regressions):
- Functional regressions: end-to-end metric drop (task-specific) > 3 percentage points or > 5% relative drop.
- Embedding drift: average cosine similarity to baseline embedding set decreases by > 5%.
- Latency regressions: p95 token latency increases by > 15% vs baseline.
- Cost/perf regressions: tokens/sec drops > 10% or GPU memory increases > 8%.
- Safety regressions: toxic/hallucination rate increases by > 1 percentage point or 20% relative.

Eval harness onboarding checklist (minimum gating before model variant is eligible for rollout):
1. Add model to the eval-harness registry (eval-harness/config/models.yaml) with metadata: model_name, commit, backbone, precision, quantization_profile (if any), supported_max_seq.
2. Create an onboarding PR that includes: updated model metadata, expected performance baselines, and CI config to run the full eval suite.
3. Run smoke suite locally: `./tools/eval/run_smoke.sh --model <model>` (should pass within 10m).
4. Run full eval suite in CI: coverage must include prompt sets for every supported product feature (chat, completions, embeddings).
5. Verify artifact reproducibility: attach model digest and sample outputs (seeded) in the PR.
6. Add owner and reviewers to the PR and publish an onboarding note in the model onboarding folder.

Prompt sets & benchmark guidelines:
- Prompt taxonomy: include at minimum: functional (task-specific), robustness (typos, paraphrase), safety (sensitive content prompts), adversarial (targeted failure modes), and calibration (confidence/uncertainty checks).
- Format: store prompts in JSONL with fields: id, split (train/dev/test), prompt, expected_output(s), tags, difficulty. Example line:
  {"id":"qa-001", "split":"test", "prompt":"Who wrote "Pride and Prejudice"?", "expected_output":"Jane Austen", "tags":["qa","canonical"]}
- Benchmark suites: create named suites (e.g., `core-chat-v1`, `summarization-robustness-v2`, `embeddings-semantic-similarity-v1`) and register them in eval-harness/config/benchmarks.yaml.
- Evaluation metrics: use task-appropriate metrics; for generation tasks prefer BLEU/ROUGE/chrF where appropriate and human-calibrated quality scores for open-ended tasks; for structured outputs use exact-match/F1; for embeddings use recall@k and average cosine similarity.
- Review cadence: prompt sets must be reviewed quarterly by the owning product team and the applied-ml team; keep a changelog with rationale for modifications.

Model onboarding step-by-step (detailed):
1. Pre-onboarding: run local profiling to collect baseline perf (latency p50/p95, memory, tokens/sec) using `perf/profiler --model <model> --seq-lens 32,128,512`.
2. Baseline eval: run `ci/evals/full_suite --model <model> --baseline-ref <golden-model>` and capture metrics into a CSV artifact.
3. Quantization profile staging (if applicable): generate candidate profiles using `quant/propose-profiles --model <model> --target=int8` and store them under `quantization-profiles/<model>/`.
4. Validation: run the quantized variant through a validation harness that includes: functional tests (full_suite), safety tests (toxicity benchmarks), and a set of latency/cost microbenchmarks.
5. Rollout plan: define canary (1%), burst (10%), wide (100%) steps with success criteria for each stage (no metric regressions beyond thresholds listed above).
6. Release: include rollout policy in config (redwood/rollouts/<model>-policy.yaml) and schedule a 24h monitoring window with dedicated dashboard.

Quality guardrails (automated + manual):
- Automated:
  - CI gating: all candidate model PRs must pass functional, safety, and integration tests, and must not exceed allowed metric regression thresholds.
  - Monitoring alerts: create per-model alerts for the key signals listed above (functional_metric_drop, embedding_drift, latency_p95_increase, safety_rate_increase).
- Manual:
  - Pre-release human signoff for any model that changes tokenization, training-data mix, or architecture.
  - Quarterly spot-checks: random sampling of generated outputs reviewed by applied-ml and product SMEs.

Quantization profiles and validation checklist:
- Profile structure (example YAML snippet):
  name: int8-rwkv-like
  method: per-channel
  calibration_dataset: eval/quant-calibration/core-1k.jsonl
  clipping: symmetric
  blocked_layers: ["lm-head"]
  notes: "Aggressive profile for latency-sensitive endpoints"

- Validation checklist:
  1. Functional parity: delta on core functional metrics <= thresholds.
  2. Safety parity: no increase in toxic output rate beyond threshold.
  3. Embedding alignment: mean cosine similarity >= 0.95 of baseline.
  4. Perf: p95 latency improvement or acceptable tradeoff documented.
  5. Memory: peak GPU memory <= baseline - expected_savings (document expected_savings).

Regression triage playbook (on alert):
1. Acknowledge alert and post to #oncall-evals with model name, alert metric, and link to dashboard.
2. Run diagnostic snapshot (automated): `ci/evals/snapshot --model <model> --since 24h --output /tmp/snapshot-<model>.tar.gz`. Attach snapshot to the incident ticket.
3. Reproduce locally: check out the exact model digest and run `./tools/eval/run_regression_check.sh --snapshot /tmp/snapshot-<model>.tar.gz`.
4. Narrow failure scope: run the full eval suite only on the changed inputs (regression-diff sets) and the last good golden baseline to compute deltas.
5. Determine root cause candidate buckets:
   a) Data drift (input distribution shift)
   b) Model change (weights, tokenization, model config)
   c) Quantization/packaging issue (incorrect scale/clipping)
   d) Infra/perf (GPU drivers, kernel regression)
   e) Upstream dependency change (tokenizer, tokenizer files, libs)
6. If model change is suspected: revert to previous model variant in the traffic routing policy and promote a rollback build in CI.
7. If quantization issue is suspected: rollback to fp16 variant and mark the quantization profile as quarantined in `quantization-profiles/quarantine.yaml`.
8. Communication: send a status update to stakeholders within 60 minutes and post a summary to #product-evals within 4 hours.
9. Postmortem and corrective action: create a postmortem if rollback or customer impact occurred; include corrective tasks and assign owners.

CI & automation patterns (practical snippets):
- CI job names: `evals/full_suite`, `evals/smoke`, `quant/validate`, `perf/profiler`. Each job must produce structured JSON artifacts that include metrics and sample outputs.
- Example CI expectation JSON (CLI output):
  {
    "model": "model-x",
    "run_id": "2026-02-10-15:22",
    "metrics": {"qa_exact_match": 0.832, "toxicity_rate": 0.012},
    "artifacts": ["/artifacts/model-x/metrics.csv", "/artifacts/model-x/samples.jsonl"]
  }
- Automated regression check (recommended): nightly job `evals/regression_check` compares latest model variants to the golden baseline and files a ticket when thresholds are exceeded.

Postmortem template (minimum):
- Summary (what happened)
- Detection (who/what alerted)
- Impact (affected endpoints/customers/metrics)
- Root cause (investigation results)
- Timeline (key events)
- Corrective actions & owners
- Preventive actions (tests, alerts, process changes)

Appendix: useful commands and locations
- Eval harness repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/eval-harness
- Models registry: eval-harness/config/models.yaml
- Benchmark registry: eval-harness/config/benchmarks.yaml
- Quant profiles: quantization-profiles/<model>/ (staging) and quantization-profiles/quarantine.yaml
- Profiling tool: `perf/profiler --help`
- Local smoke: `./tools/eval/run_smoke.sh --model <model>`
- Regression snapshot: `ci/evals/snapshot`
